name: Church Government
overview: Scripture reveals that all authority ultimately belongs to God, who is the sovereign governor over nations (Psalms 22:28) and ordains powers according to His will (Romans 13:1). Jesus affirms that earthly authority operates only by divine permission (John 19:11), yet believers are called to obey God above human rulers when the two are in conflict (Acts 5:29). The New Testament church practices government through appointed elders and overseers, who are entrusted by the Holy Spirit to shepherd and care for the church purchased by Christ's blood (Acts 14:23; Acts 20:28). This framework underscores a God-centered, Spirit-led structure for church leadership and submission to divine authority.
